title: Finite proper normalization with refinement and quotient compatibility
statement:
Fix the finite-field datum $(p,a,q,k_0,k)$ of [def-weil-finite-field-fiber], a prime $\ell\ne p$, and an algebraic closure $\Omega=\overline{\mathbf Q}_\ell$. Let $E\subset\Omega$ be a finite extension of $\mathbf Q_\ell$, with valuation ring $R=\mathcal O_E$, uniformizer $t=\varpi_E$, and $A_n=R/t^n$ for $n\ge1$ [def-weil-l-adic-coefficient-extension]. Let $X,Y$ be separated finite-type $k$-schemes and $f:X\to Y$ a proper $k$-morphism [def-weil-scheme-morphism-properties, def-weil-proper-morphism]. Use the small pro-etale sites, finite constructible categories, derived direct images and compact-support candidates of [def-compact-support-direct-image-detailed, def-weil-derived-direct-image]. Write $c_0=(\operatorname{id}_X,f)$ for the identity compactification [def-weil-compactifications-refinements].

Let $a_n:(\operatorname{id}_X)_!\xrightarrow{\sim}\operatorname{id}$ denote the sectionwise identity identification for extension by zero [def-weil-extension-by-zero]. Put $\alpha_n^0=Rf_{*,n}(a_n):Rf_{!,n}^{c_0}\xrightarrow{\sim}Rf_{*,n}$. For any compactification $c$ of $f$, compose the canonical common-refinement comparison $C_{c,c_0,n}$ with $\alpha_n^0$ and denote the resulting comparison by $\alpha_n^c$. On $D^b_c(X,A_n)$ this is a natural isomorphism, independent of the common refinement, and
$$\alpha_n^{c'}\circ C_{c,c',n}=\alpha_n^c.$$
Bounded constructible inputs lie in the etale-origin domain required for these comparisons [lem-sf-proetale-constructible-origin, prop-compactification-coherence-detailed]. At $c_0$, for every quotient $\varphi:A_{n+1}\twoheadrightarrow A_n$, the square
$$\rho_{*,\varphi}\circ(\alpha_{n+1}^0\operatorname{Res}_{\varphi})=(\operatorname{Res}_{\varphi}\alpha_n^0)\circ\rho_{!,\varphi}$$
commutes on $D(X_{\mathrm{proet}},A_n)$, where $\rho_!$ is exactly the open-extension/ordinary-direct-image restriction comparison of [lem-sf-compact-support-restriction-of-scalars] and $\rho_*$ its ordinary direct-image factor. These identities are natural in the input and compatible with successive quotient homomorphisms.

proof.text: The identity normalization is the published derived identity-open isomorphism whiskered by ordinary direct image, then the left unitor. It is defined on all unbounded inputs.

For a bounded constructible K choose bounds a,b from its bounded cohomological support and use [min a b,max a b] as a vanishing interval. The finite-ring constructible derived origin theorem gives a bounded constructible etale L and a realization isomorphism. Its lower bound makes L an object of the plus category. The exact functor compositor gives the specified realization coordinates.
Unfold properFiniteComparison as C(c,c0) followed by the identity normalization. Associativity and the published cocycle C(c,c′)C(c′,c0)=C(c,c0) prove the asserted refinement equation.

The identity-open scalar restriction lemma identifies a_A Res with b followed by Res a_B. Whisker this equality by ordinary direct image. Naturality of sfDerivedImageRestriction at a_B identifies the composite with sfCompactSupportRestriction followed by the restricted normalization, proving the quotient square for any finite-ring map.

Use sfCompactSupportRestriction_comp for the compact-support successive quotient equation, with prime invertibility furnished by the finite coefficient setting. Naturality of the normalization at the source coefficient associator and of the target coefficient associator at the normalization allows the three quotient squares to be pasted. Substitute the compact-support cocycle and cancel the invertible source normalization, obtaining the ordinary direct-image cocycle. The generic quotient square supplies the composite square.
